From the supplied comparison, these are the **four highest-priority visible geometry corrections**:

1. **Hood–fender transition remains too angular.** The model has pronounced raised fender ridges bordering a flat, trapezoidal hood, with abrupt folds into the nose corners. The photograph shows broader, softer transitions and a more continuously rounded nose. **Reduce the ridge height, widen the transition surfaces, and round the front corners**, rather than simply smoothing the existing sharp boundaries.

2. **Wheels dominate the side silhouette; the axle span looks short relative to the body.** The model’s wheels occupy more of the body height, while substantial bodywork extends beyond both axles. Its wheel spokes also remain narrow and skeletal compared with the photograph’s broader, sculpted five-part faces. **Trial a modest reduction in overall wheel diameter, broaden/deepen the spoke surfaces, and rebalance axle spacing versus overhangs.** Establish a camera-matched overlay before committing to wheelbase changes—the approximate profile views cannot establish exact dimensions.

3. **Rear-quarter mass and tail taper are misplaced.** In the model, the rear deck reads as a long, nearly horizontal shelf above the rear wheel; the photograph has a more flowing roof-to-quarter transition and a tighter, tapering tail. **Reshape the rear haunch as a continuous volume, then taper the upper and lower tail surfaces toward the rear**, reducing the squared-off shelf effect. Judge the final tail length only after matching viewpoint.

4. **Rear bumper and machinery housing are too flat and diagrammatic.** The model’s machinery sits in a shallow-looking rectangular enclosure, with simple circular mouths. The photograph shows a deeper, rounded-shouldered housing, stronger recesses around the lower machinery, and more substantial bumper returns beside it. **Rebuild the enclosure’s cross-section and depth, round its upper shoulders, recess the lower units, and add thickness to the surrounding bumper volumes.** Enlarging the circles alone will not resolve this.

**Camera/crop limits:** The rear photograph cannot establish the wing or complete upper-rear silhouette because of its crop; the stowed wing is not counted as an error. Perspective also affects apparent track width, wheelbase, and overhangs. The surface-transition and machinery-depth discrepancies are more defensible than exact proportional corrections from these views.
